BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall read.** The Seller Update is a near-uniform departure from our playbook on every liability, disclosure and completion-mechanics point. Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter is considerably more candid than the Update: it concedes no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay receipt/assignment, bonuses missing from the funds flow, and an unresolved incident. We should use the Disclosure Letter's admissions against the Update's characterisations ("addressed", "settled", "adequate", "not expected to be material"), none of which are verified facts or agreed positions.

---

## A. Liability regime

**1. General cap – cl 12.1 (20% / AUD 4.8m).**
Departs from our 25% / AUD 6.0m starting position. The 20% figure happens to match our conditional fallback, but that fallback is usable *only* with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given. The number matching is not clearance. **Push back: reinstate 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**

**2. Thresholds – cl 12.2.**
- De minimis AUD 25,000 vs our AUD 5,000 (5x).
- Basket AUD 250,000 vs our AUD 50,000 (5x).
- "Excess only" vs our first-dollar ("tipping") recovery.
Combined effect strips a material band of ordinary warranty claims entirely. **Push back: AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar once exceeded.**

**3. Claims period – cl 12.3/13 (18 months).**
Departs from 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval — not given. **Push back: 24 months.**

**4. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13), and cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 applying limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature".**
This is the hidden general-regime override the playbook warns about. As drafted it would sweep Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and specific indemnities (Ironquay) into the 20% cap, 18-month period and basket, and would purport to limit fraud. **Push back:**
- Delete the default "applies to all Claims" language; limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims as expressly listed.
- Express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-negotiable and no deal-team member may waive it.
- Keep Title / Tax / IP / payment / covenant categories as separate regimes.

**5. Fundamental / Title warranties on general caps "for administrative simplicity".**
Reject outright. **Require:** separate regime, 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

## B. Disclosure and knowledge

**6. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – whole data room, statutory registers, public records deemed disclosed.**
Direct conflict with the playbook. A blanket data-room disclosure makes the warranties near-worthless given the volume of DD-002 to DD-012. **Push back:** disclosure only if specifically and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; delete general data-room, public-register and "prudent search" disclosure. Note [1.4] (no admissions) — fine in itself, but it confirms that nothing in the letter can be relied on as a Seller concession of consent/payment requirements either, so our own covenants must do the work.

**7. Cl 8.3 – blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records.**
Delete. "Discoverable" is worse than actual knowledge — it imports a constructive-knowledge bar on top of deemed disclosure. If any qualifier survives, it must be: actual knowledge of named buyer individuals only (we should resist even that); and in no circumstances applicable to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Seller knowledge qualifiers in the warranties should be limited to named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry.

## C. Completion mechanics and conditions

**8. Bluefen – cl 3 / 6.3.**
Update says "addressed"; Disclosure Letter [2] confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue — a material customer. "Reasonable endeavours" plus consent-on-delivery is insufficient. **Require:** condition precedent that effective Bluefen consent is obtained *and* written evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; buyer right to review form of consent; no deemed satisfaction on mere delivery.

**9. Riverlark – cl 2 / 7.**
Post-completion release is contrary to playbook; Disclosure Letter [3] confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, no repayment, no discharge, and change-control at cl 8.1 (so the sale itself may trigger default). **Require:** current payout letter before Completion; repayment direct from Completion funds per the funds flow; executed security releases/PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking *and* Amelia Frost approval — neither exists.

**10. Employee bonuses – DD-005 / funds flow.**
Seller says the AUD 420,000 is "a matter for the Seller" but the funds flow does not itemise it, and Disclosure Letter [5] confirms on-costs (super, payroll tax) are unaddressed. Because these are Company obligations triggered by Completion, silence means the Buyer funds them post-Completion. **Require:** specific line item (bonuses plus triggered super/payroll tax/other on-costs) deducted from the price or paid by Seller at Completion, with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall. The funds flow must not be presented as "agreed" — it is not.

**11. Ironquay IP – cl 11.1.**
Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment is too narrow: the risk is that Project Materials have not transferred (DD-004 cl 7.3), not merely the fee. The AUD 180,000 (DD-010) is unverified either way — not proof of non-payment, but no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. **Require:** broadened indemnity covering loss from any failure of title/transfer of SOW3 (and related) Project Materials and third-party IP claims, preserving the SOW3 cure (payment of outstanding fees triggers transfer); pre-Completion deliverable of payment receipt and confirmatory assignment, or escrow; verify the AUD 180,000 against bank records.

## D. Diligence matters

**12. Export/privacy incident – DD-006 / cl 4.6 / Sch 6.**
"Not expected to be material" is a Seller assertion, not a finding. Position consistently with playbook: assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric exposure in either direction. **Require:** pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete and document the investigation, provide regular updates and the final report; specific indemnity (outside general cap/basket) for loss from the incident; warranty that there are no other known incidents. Do not characterise it as material ourselves.

**13. Sandbar renewals – DD-008/DD-011 (AUD 330,000).**
Seller asserts "ordinary course"; the Disclosure Letter [8] admits it does not establish whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Assess — no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. **Action:** request the contracts, read DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing/scope; if accrued and unavoidable pre-Completion, treat via working-capital/accruals rather than asserting Debt.

**14. Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime".**
Not agreed. These remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Tax and IP must sit in separate regimes (separate caps and periods, outside general basket) — to be negotiated. Push back on any suggestion of settlement.

**15. Title – DD-012.**
The share register is a Seller-supplied internal source; Disclosure Letter [10] itself concedes Buyer verification is incomplete. **Require:** independent evidence — ASIC company search, PPSR search, certificate of registration/constitution, board minutes/authority evidence, encumbrance confirmations (including Riverlark security over shares), and a title warranty on the fundamental regime.

**16. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).**
Lower risk on the Seller's own description (notification only; assignment restriction not triggered by share sale) but we should read the provisions ourselves rather than accept the characterisation; include a pre-Completion notification covenant for the lease.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cap | 20% / 4.8m | 25% / 6.0m — no Frost authority for fallback |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess only | 5k / 50k / first dollar |
| 3 | Period | 18 months | 24 months — no Frost approval for fallback |
| 4 | Scope of limitations | All Claims of any nature | General Warranty Claims only; separate Title/Tax/IP/covenant regimes; absolute fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out |
| 5 | Title/Fundamental | Same as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + registers | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Delete; never for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence conditions met |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | Payout, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not itemised | Line item incl. on-costs, seller-funded |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Broaden; preserve cure; verify 180k |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Preserve logs, investigate, updates, specific indemnity; no assumed breach |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess; no automatic Debt/price deduction |
| 14 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | OPEN; separate regimes |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence required |

**Process points:** Nothing in these documents is "agreed", "final" or "market" merely because the Seller says so. No fallback should be conceded without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing the specific draft. Recommend we respond with a full mark-up reinstating the playbook positions and a deliverables list (Bluefen consent + conditions evidence, Riverlark payout and releases, Ironquay receipt/assignment, incident report, Sandbar contracts, independent title searches) before any further movement on economics.
